headline: Attackers pounced on a max-severity SAP Commerce Cloud flaw within three days of its patch as France's tax agency and oil giant Shell confronted fresh data-theft claims.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep weaponizing enterprise flaws within days of disclosure, hitting a max-severity SAP Commerce Cloud bug three days after its patch shipped.
emerging_trends.topic_title: SAP Commerce Cloud Flaw Under Active Exploitation

emerging_trends.text: The tools defenders trust became the attack surface, as analysis traced the compromise of 2,500 organizations to the Trivy scanner, with most victims exposed well before the blamed LiteLLM packages surfaced.
Data theft dominated the day's incidents, from France's tax agency admitting a breach a hacker ties to 600,000 victims to Shell probing Clop's 89-gigabyte extortion claim.
emerging_trends.topic_title: France Tax Breach and Shell Clop Claim

topics.title: Compliance and Post-Quantum Deadlines Advance
topics.latest_developments: Google Cloud published a post-quantum cryptography roadmap targeting 2029 readiness with milestones in 2027 and 2028, AWS Certificate Manager set 2027 to phase out email-validated certificate renewals ahead of the CA/Browser Forum's March 15, 2028 cutoff, and Europe opened 17 draft Cyber Resilience Act standards for comment.
topics.summary: The moves push enterprises toward quantum-resistant encryption, stronger certificate validation, and Cyber Resilience Act conformity, whose connected-product rules bind manufacturers by the end of 2027.

sources.title: Google Cloud Sets Out Post-Quantum Roadmap With 2029 Readiness Goal
AWS Certificate Manager sets 2027 end date for email-validated certificate renewals
17 draft Cyber Resilience Act standards are open for comment

topics.title: France Tax Breach and Shell Clop Claim
topics.latest_developments: France confirmed intruders reached the Directorate General of Public Finances in late June by stealing or misusing an identity, while a hacker claims 600,000 victims, and Shell opened an investigation after the Clop gang claimed it stole 89 gigabytes of data.
topics.summary: France's tax authority, the DGFiP, is probing the June intrusion, and oil giant Shell is examining Clop's extortion claim; neither has confirmed the full scope.

sources.title: France investigates tax authority breach after hacker claims 600,000 victims
Shell investigates 'potential incident' after Clop data theft claims

topics.title: SAP Commerce Cloud Flaw Under Active Exploitation
topics.latest_developments: Threat intelligence firm Defused reports attackers began targeting a maximum-severity SAP Commerce Cloud remote code execution flaw just three days after SAP patched it.
topics.summary: The vulnerability lets attackers run code on SAP Commerce Cloud e-commerce deployments; administrators should apply SAP's fix immediately.

sources.title: Max severity SAP Commerce Cloud flaw now targeted in attacks

topics.title: Trivy Scanner Drives 2,500-Org Compromise
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reports the open-source scanner Trivy drove the compromise of 2,500 organizations, with over 95 percent of them exposed before the malicious LiteLLM packages first blamed ever appeared.
topics.summary: Investigators traced the mass compromise to Trivy exposure across enterprises; affected organizations should review how they deploy the scanner.

sources.title: Trivy, Not LiteLLM Behind the 2,500 Org Compromise

topics.title: Cyera Buys Oasis for AI Agent Identity Control
topics.latest_developments: Cyera agreed to buy Oasis Security for $1 billion to merge data security and identity into one control plane for AI agents, redefining privileged access around business context in place of static roles.
topics.summary: The deal targets the governance gap as enterprises deploy autonomous AI agents that need scoped, monitored access to data and systems.

sources.title: Cyera's Oasis Security Buy is All About AI Agent Control

topics.title: Flock Tightens License-Plate Privacy Controls
topics.latest_developments: Flock Safety will require every customer to turn on its Audit Assistance feature for flagging abnormal searches and will hold most license-plate data for only seven days, answering scandals over officer abuse.
topics.summary: Flock Safety runs a nationwide automated license-plate reader network used by police departments; the new controls follow reports of officers misusing the system.

sources.title: Flock tightens privacy controls amid scandals over officer abuse

business.title: Leetsdale Faith-Based Boxing Gym Falls Through
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported August 14 that organizers pulled the plan after they could not satisfy Leetsdale borough ordinances.
business.summary: A proposed faith-based boxing gym in Leetsdale, a borough in Allegheny County's Sewickley area, will not open; the organizers abandoned the project after finding no way to comply with borough ordinances.

sources.title: Proposed Leetsdale boxing club no longer happening

business.title: Derry Pool Rebounds on Higher Lifeguard Pay
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported August 14 that the Derry Community Pool ran a smooth 2026 season after raising lifeguard pay.
business.summary: Derry Borough Mayor Nathan Bundy said the Derry Community Pool in Westmoreland County operated smoothly all summer on strong attendance and higher lifeguard wages, reversing 2025, when a lifeguard shortage forced the pool to close on several days.

sources.title: Derry Community Pool bounces back from lifeguard shortage with higher pay, strong attendance

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Funds Free Menstrual Products in Schools
around_town.latest_developments: WTAE reported August 14 that Pennsylvania will spend $9 million over three years to place free menstrual products in schools.
around_town.summary: Pennsylvania is directing $9 million over the next three years to supply free menstrual products in its public schools, a program the state frames as attacking "period poverty" among students.

sources.title: New state funding aims to combat 'period poverty' among Pennsylvania students

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Game Commission Ends Deputy Warden Program
around_town.latest_developments: WPXI reported August 14 that the Pennsylvania Game Commission will officially end its Deputy Game Warden Program on September 1.
around_town.summary: The Pennsylvania Game Commission is closing its Deputy Game Warden Program, which embedded volunteer deputies within law enforcement, effective September 1, 2026.

sources.title: Pennsylvania Game Commission ending Deputy Game Warden Program with law enforcement

around_town.title: North Allegheny Opens 2026-27 Year August 18
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported August 14 that North Allegheny School District begins classes August 18 with a larger student body.
around_town.summary: North Allegheny School District, north of Pittsburgh, starts its 2026-27 school year on August 18, 2026, adding enrollment along with new and returning staff.

sources.title: It's back to school time at North Allegheny: Here's what's new for 2026-27

around_teams.title: Steelers Quarterbacks Impress in Preseason Debut
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette and TribLive coverage August 13-14 praised Drew Allar, Will Howard, and Mason Rudolph and the new-look passing attack after Aaron Rodgers sat out.
around_teams.summary: With Aaron Rodgers resting, quarterbacks Drew Allar, Will Howard, and Mason Rudolph each moved the Steelers' offense in Mike McCarthy's preseason opener against Green Bay; Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles wrote the team's new passing scheme made a strong first impression, and TribLive said the Allar hype train had left the station.

sources.title: Steelers QBs all start off on the right foot in preseason win over the Packers
Noah Hiles: The Steelers' new passing scheme makes a strong first impression

around_teams.title: Rookie Germie Bernard Shines in NFL Debut
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported August 14 that rookie receiver Germie Bernard made plays and "doesn't blink" in his first NFL action.
around_teams.summary: Steelers rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard drew praise for a composed preseason debut against the Packers, catching passes and settling into the offense without visible nerves, the Post-Gazette reported.

sources.title: Steelers rookie receiver Germie Bernard 'doesn't blink' in his NFL debut

reading.author: Stratechery
reading.title: Anthropic's Watermarking, How It (Probably) Works, Worse Than It Seems
reading.summary: Ben Thompson argues that Anthropic's move to watermark AI output in response to the European Union's AI law is a mistake, chiefly on philosophical grounds, and that the mechanism works worse than its backers claim.

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: Don't Look Up
reading.summary: Zitron argues that investors, executives, and the press keep refusing to confront mounting warning signs around the AI buildout, extending his running case that the sector rests on unsustainable spending.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: On AI Coding and Its Discontents
reading.summary: Newport uses the account of a senior Silicon Valley engineer, a self-described AI skeptic turned convert, to weigh what AI coding tools actually change about software work and where their limits lie.
